script: They go for about $50,000 today: rally history, but only 160 horsepower. It's Audi's original 1985 Quattro. In 1981, Michèle Mouton won the Sanremo world championship rally driving a Quattro. No woman had won before. Its 2.1-liter turbocharged inline-five sends 160 horsepower and 210 pound-feet of torque through a five-speed manual to all four wheels. Audi built just 11,452 original Quattros during the entire 1980 - 1991 run, and each was assembled by hand. Under that factory spoiler sits a steel trunk lid; Audi didn't switch to fiberglass until September 1987. The engine pairs an iron block with an aluminum head and uses an air-to-air intercooler to cool the turbo's compressed intake air. You operate the center and rear differential locks from the cabin through vacuum servos, rather than letting a computer decide. So would you spend fifty grand on 160 horsepower for the car that helped change rallying forever?

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 1985 Audi Quattro, finished in Alpine White with a black interior, and will be displayed at the Cars & Bids Larz Anderson Auto Museum Meetup on Saturday, June 27th, 2026. The attached Carfax vehicle history report contains some gaps, though it shows no mileage discrepancies during the given time period. A partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes 15-inch wheels, locking center and rear differentials, a rear spoiler, a sunroof, leather upholstery, heated front seats, and air conditioning. Notable modifications reported by the seller are limited to an Alpine head unit. Celebrated as one of the most emblematic German cars of the 1980s, the Audi Quattro arrived for 1983 as a rally-bred evolution of the Coupe. It stood out from its front-wheel-drive sibling with a specific body kit, a turbocharged engine, and a full-time four-wheel drive system. Executives never envisioned the Quattro as a volume model, so only a small handful were brought to America between 1983 and 1985, but the coupe left a significant mark on the Audi range: it's the car from which every RS model traces its roots. Power comes from a 2.1-liter turbocharged inline-5, rated at 160 horsepower and 210 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to all four wheels via a 5-speed manual transmission.
